summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with acute gastrointestinal bleeding and heart failure exacerbation, presenting with melena, hypotension, and dyspnea. He had a history of recurrent GI bleeding on anticoagulation for a mechanical aortic valve. Warfarin was held and heparin bridged due to high stroke risk. He received multiple blood transfusions for hemoglobin dropping to 6.6 g/dL. Endoscopy and capsule study identified gastric and small bowel angiodysplasias as the likely source, with colonoscopy showing diverticulosis but no active bleeding. He was managed conservatively with pantoprazole, sucralfate, and iron supplementation. Heart failure was treated with IV diuresis, transitioning to oral torsemide, with improvement in volume status and weight reduction to 78 kg. A PICC line was placed for ongoing transfusion access. Warfarin was restarted at a lower target INR of 2.0–3.0. He was discharged home with services, on a plan for weekly pheresis unit transfusions, close INR and hemoglobin monitoring, and follow-up with cardiology and gastroenterology for possible APC therapy.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, with hemorrhage
Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Angiodysplasia of stomach and duodenum without mention of hemorrhage
Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Heart valve replaced by other means
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
